facts.statement: The genus Amelacanthus was described by Maisey in 1982.
The genus Amelacanthus contains four described species.
Amelacanthus is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish belonging to the elasmobranchs.
facts.quote: Amelacanthus is an extinct genus of elasmobranchian cartilaginous fish

facts.statement: Fossils of Amelacanthus have been found in North America, Europe, and Africa during the Carboniferous and Permian periods.
facts.quote: It is known from the Permian and Carboniferous of North America, Europe, and Africa

facts.statement: Specimens of Amelacanthus are known from the Famennian stage in Russia.
facts.quote: It is also known from the Famennian of Russia

facts.statement: Amelacanthus fossils have been discovered in Oman from the Wordian stage of the Permian and the Induan stage of the Triassic.
facts.quote: Specimens of Amelacanthus have additionally been found in Permian (Wordian) and Triassic (Induan) sediments of Oman

facts.statement: Amelacanthus is one of the few Ctenacanth fish to survive the Permian-Triassic extinction event, though it went extinct shortly thereafter in the Early Triassic.
facts.quote: This makes Amelacanthus one of the only known Ctenacanths to have survived (albeit only briefly) the Permian-Trassic extinction event, going extinct only in the Early Triassic

facts.statement: The genus Amelacanthus is known primarily from fin spines.
facts.quote: It is known from fin spines
